content.content:
=== V4__invoices.sql ===
-- Invoices: an amount billed on a project. Each invoice belongs to one project
-- (project_id -> projects.id), so a project's detail page lists ITS invoices and totals them.
CREATE TABLE invoices (
    id         BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    project_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id),
    amount     NUMERIC(12, 2) NOT NULL
);
=== V6__invoices_amount_positive.sql ===
-- An invoice must bill a positive amount — you cannot raise an invoice for nothing. Enforce it at
-- the DB level too, matching the server + front-end validation: rejects zero and negative amounts,
-- so no bad row can slip in through any path.
ALTER TABLE invoices
    ADD CONSTRAINT invoices_amount_positive CHECK (amount > 0);
=== V9__invoices_status_draft_default.sql ===
-- Invoices now move through a lifecycle: DRAFT -> SENT -> PAID. A freshly raised invoice starts as a
-- DRAFT (it is sent later, which is what records an audit entry and unlocks payment), so the column
-- default becomes DRAFT. Existing rows keep whatever status they already hold.
ALTER TABLE invoices ALTER COLUMN status SET DEFAULT 'DRAFT';
=== V12__tasks.sql ===
-- Tasks: a checklist item on a project. Each task belongs to one project (project_id -> projects.id)
-- and is either OPEN (done = FALSE, the default) or DONE (done = TRUE), ticked off as work completes.
CREATE TABLE tasks (
    id         BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    project_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id),
    title      VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    done       BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE
);

===POM (db deps)===
  H2 + Flyway + Actuator. Coordinates VERIFIED against OfficeFloor tutorials
         data-jpa (H2 access for services), actuator (health probe). -->
    <!-- Bean Validation provider (Hibernate Validator) — OfficeFloor REST / Spring bind + @Valid. -->
    <!-- In-memory H2 + Flyway schema migrations on boot (Spring-managed). -->
      <groupId>com.h2database</groupId>
      <artifactId>h2</artifactId>
      <groupId>org.flywaydb</groupId>
      <artifactId>flyway-core</artifactId>
    <!-- REQUIRED under Spring Boot 4: FlywayAutoConfiguration was extracted from
         spring-boot-autoconfigure into this module. Without it, flyway-core is on the classpath but
         managed by the parent BOM. Found via the cp01 dry run. flyway-core 12.x has H2 support
         built in, so no flyway-database-h2 module is needed. -->
      <artifactId>spring-boot-flyway</artifactId>
===stack.yaml===
# What this STACK is, for the harness (~/ui-long-degradation-test). Read at `base-empty`, never
# from the working tree, so a run always measures the layers the base declared.
#
# The layer source roots live HERE rather than in the harness config for the same reason `--repo`
# does: one harness drives many stacks, and a harness-level glob like
# `src/main/frontend/**/*.{ts,tsx}` silently matches NOTHING for a stack whose front-end is
# templates or `.svelte` — every `frontend_*` column then reads 0/None, which looks like an answer.
#
# `ext` says which files ARE this layer's source. It does not promise they are parseable: a layer
# Lizard cannot read still gets every git-derived metric (hot_surface, reedit_line_stats, impact
# addition/mutation split), and its parser-derived columns come back blank instead of zero.
#
# GENERATED CODE MUST BE GITIGNORED (see .gitignore): the metrics read committed trees and diffs,
# so anything ignored is simply absent. Here that is `routeTree.gen.ts` (TanStack Router generates
# it from routes/) and `src/main/resources/static/` (the vite build output).
layers:
  frontend:
    root: src/main/frontend
    ext: [ts, tsx]
    # jscpd's language for this layer's duplication metrics (dup_*) — declared here because the
    # harness cannot guess it, and a wrong/absent value yields blanks rather than a silent zero.
    jscpd_format: typescript,tsx
    # The layer's ENTRY SURFACE, as a regex over "<file>::<function>". Anchors the role-comparable
    # handler metrics (entry_cc, wmc_handler, erosion_handler) to the unit a new feature enters
    # through: here the file-based route components. `wmc_max` reports whatever the heaviest file
    # happens to be, which is not the same thing across stacks.
    handler_pattern: "/routes/[^:]*::"
    # The declared ADDITIVE unit, for fnpkg_* (count rises while size stays flat = healthy
    # additive growth; size climbing = the unit is absorbing rules).
    function_package_glob: "src/main/frontend/features/**/*.slot.tsx"
  backend:
    root: src/main/java
    ext: [java]
    jscpd_format: java
    # Every OfficeFloor logic class reached through a `service(...)` method.
    handler_pattern: "::service$"
    # Non-blank, non-comment YAML lines of the wiring, counted separately (config_loc) and never
    # mixed into an erosion or verbosity denominator.
    config_globs: ["src/main/resources/officefloor/**/*.yml"]
    # One wired node per endpoint: this arm declares a YAML file per route, so the node roots come
    # from a GLOB rather than one wiring file. Drives node_cc_median — the complexity a developer
    # loads to change one rule — and node_exclusive_share, how much of it each node owns alone.
    node_roots:
      wiring_glob: "src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/**/*.yml"
      class_regex: 'class:\s*([\w.]+)'
      node_method: service
===Application===
package net.officefloor.hq.app;

import org.springframework.boot.SpringApplication;
import org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.SpringBootApplication;

/**
 * Spring Boot 4 host. OfficeFloor REST is added by the officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter on
 * the classpath; domain endpoints are declared as additive OfficeFloor YAML under
 * src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/*.GET.yml (each -> a logic class with a service(...) method).
 * Spring serves the SPA (static/), H2 + Flyway + Actuator.
 *
 * At the base this is a bare shell; checkpoints add migrations, officefloor/rest routes + logic,
 * @Service beans, and front-end features.
 */
@SpringBootApplication
public class Application {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        SpringApplication.run(Application.class, args);
    }
}

# What this STACK is, for the harness (~/ui-long-degradation-test). Read at `base-empty`, never
# from the working tree, so a run always measures the layers the base declared.
#
# The layer source roots live HERE rather than in the harness config for the same reason `--repo`
# does: one harness drives many stacks, and a harness-level glob like
# `src/main/frontend/**/*.{ts,tsx}` silently matches NOTHING for a stack whose front-end is
# templates or `.svelte` — every `frontend_*` column then reads 0/None, which looks like an answer.
#
# `ext` says which files ARE this layer's source. It does not promise they are parseable: a layer
# Lizard cannot read still gets every git-derived metric (hot_surface, reedit_line_stats, impact
# addition/mutation split), and its parser-derived columns come back blank instead of zero.
#
# GENERATED CODE MUST BE GITIGNORED (see .gitignore): the metrics read committed trees and diffs,
# so anything ignored is simply absent. Here that is `routeTree.gen.ts` (TanStack Router generates
# it from routes/) and `src/main/resources/static/` (the vite build output).
layers:
  frontend:
    root: src/main/frontend
    ext: [ts, tsx]
    # jscpd's language for this layer's duplication metrics (dup_*) — declared here because the
    # harness cannot guess it, and a wrong/absent value yields blanks rather than a silent zero.
    jscpd_format: typescript,tsx
    # The layer's ENTRY SURFACE, as a regex over "<file>::<function>". Anchors the role-comparable
    # handler metrics (entry_cc, wmc_handler, erosion_handler) to the unit a new feature enters
    # through: here the file-based route components. `wmc_max` reports whatever the heaviest file
    # happens to be, which is not the same thing across stacks.
    handler_pattern: "/routes/[^:]*::"
    # The declared ADDITIVE unit, for fnpkg_* (count rises while size stays flat = healthy
    # additive growth; size climbing = the unit is absorbing rules).
    function_package_glob: "src/main/frontend/features/**/*.slot.tsx"
  backend:
    root: src/main/java
    ext: [java]
    jscpd_format: java
    # Every OfficeFloor logic class reached through a `service(...)` method.
    handler_pattern: "::service$"
    # Non-blank, non-comment YAML lines of the wiring, counted separately (config_loc) and never
    # mixed into an erosion or verbosity denominator.
    config_globs: ["src/main/resources/officefloor/**/*.yml"]
    # One wired node per endpoint: this arm declares a YAML file per route, so the node roots come
    # from a GLOB rather than one wiring file. Drives node_cc_median — the complexity a developer
    # loads to change one rule — and node_exclusive_share, how much of it each node owns alone.
    node_roots:
      wiring_glob: "src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/**/*.yml"
      class_regex: 'class:\s*([\w.]+)'
      node_method: service

-- recomputed on the server every time a line is added.

content.text:
Both acceptance tests pass, the Maven build is clean, and strict `tsc` typechecking passes. Here's what I implemented for the "list what I'm charging for, work out the total" change — a full-stack, additive change:

**Database** (new Flyway migrations)
- `V13__invoice_line_items.sql` — new `invoice_line_items` table (`invoice_id` FK, `description`, `qty`, `unit_price`).
- `V14__invoices_amount_derived.sql` — drops the old "amount must be positive" constraint, since an invoice's amount is now a *derived* total (sum of its lines) and a line-less draft legitimately totals zero.

**Server** (OfficeFloor REST, all new files)
- `LineItem` entity + `LineItemRepository`.
- `GET /api/lineitems?invoiceId=` (`LineItemsGetLogic`) and `POST /api/lineitems` (`LineItemsPostLogic`) with their `.yml` wiring. Adding a line validates the input, then re-works and stores the invoice's `amount` as the sum of `qty × unit_price` across its lines — so the figure is always computed, never typed.
- `TestSupportController` seed/reset extended to insert `lineItems`, compute each invoice's `amount` from them, and truncate the new table on reset.

**Front-end** (new files + the established open-link pattern)
- `routes/invoices.tsx` layout (`<Outlet />`) and `routes/invoices.$invoiceId.tsx` detail route (drilling in is a child route, per the rules).
- `features/invoices/lineItems.ts` (query/mutation under `['lineItems', invoiceId]`, invalidating the shared `['invoices']` key so project totals stay in step), `LineItemList.tsx` (the `invoice-lineitems-table` + derived `invoice-amount` total), and `LineItemForm.tsx` (description / qty / unit-price fields).
- One minimal edit to `InvoiceList.tsx` adding the per-row `invoice-open-<id>` link — mirroring the existing `project-open-<id>` convention in `ProjectList`.

All the `data-testid` anchors the spec expects (`invoice-open-1`, `invoice-lineitems-table`, `lineitem-row-1`/`lineitem-description`, `invoice-amount`, and the `lineitem-form-*` fields) are matched, and existing testids were left untouched.
